policy_title: Promote a circular economy and right to repair
stated: Advocate for a circular economy by requiring manufacturers to offer ten-year warranties on white goods, introduce a comprehensive 'right to repair', eliminate built-in obsolescence, and mandate production of energy-efficient white goods, TVs, and lighting.

source.quote: Green MPs will advocate for a circular economy that reduces the waste of resources. We will require manufacturers to offer ten-year warranties on white goods, to encourage repair and reuse. We will introduce a comprehensive ‘right to repair’, so manufacturers keep goods operational years after purchase and to eliminate built-in obsolescence. We will require manufacturers to produce only the most energy efficient white goods, TVs, lighting and electric cookers.

bearing_set.reason: Ten-year warranties, right to repair, and elimination of built-in obsolescence reduce household replacement costs for essential white goods; mandated energy-efficient appliances directly lower energy bills — both affecting real disposable income and the household cost basket.

Mandatory energy-efficient white goods, TVs, and lighting cuts energy consumption and associated emissions; a circular economy model reduces manufacturing waste and resource extraction, with a plausible non-negligible effect on emissions trajectory and environmental quality.

Manufacturers face non-trivial compliance costs (redesign for repairability, warranty liability, energy-efficiency retooling) that could dampen investment and raise prices, while the repair sector and longer product lifecycles create countervailing economic opportunity — a genuinely contested but material effect on business dynamism and real living standards.

membership_note: Three real bearings: cost-of-living relief via lower energy bills and fewer replacements (O2); environmental gains from energy efficiency and circular-economy waste reduction (O6); and a contested aggregate-prosperity tradeoff between manufacturer compliance costs and repair-economy gains (O13). Distributional effects (O14) are real but secondary to and largely captured within the O2 channel; O10 (liberty) is not engaged as the mandates fall on manufacturers, not individuals.
